sources.title: ICANH, Abya Yala: Gunadule networks and community accounts
sources.note: Direct museum interpretation and separately attributed community testimony. Las redes Gunadule: named in Spanish records around 1610, earlier ethnic relationship uncertain, privateer alliances; community testimony preserves distinct account. Do not silently identify all Cueva archaeology as Gunadule.

sources.title: ICANH, Pueblo Gunadule
sources.note: Direct short institutional description: Colombia and Panama, Tule/Kuna names and Chibchan language.

sources.title: Ministerio de Cultura, Pueblo tule: sociolinguistic self-assessment
sources.note: Direct 110-page publication based on 2009 survey. Printed 27-29: extended matrilocal households, congress and homes; printed 32: school curriculum tensions; printed 79 language learning primarily in families. Survey-era description, not ancient universal customs.

sources.title: Ruth Virginia Castaño Carvajal and Milton Santacruz Aguilar, Ibisoge Yala Burba Mola (2016)
sources.note: Direct Museo del Oro article, printed 290-313. Printed 295 exact prose heading Anmala gunadulemala bia daniggi / ¿De dónde venimos los gunadule?; printed 298-299 ruler/pencil diagram work; protection meanings attributed to participants, no medical efficacy claim.

sources.title: Banco de la República, Mola A00660
sources.note: Indexed original museum object text: recent Darién-Gunadule blouse, 31.5 by 41.0 cm, layered cloth joined with needle and thread. No ancient date claimed.

sources.title: Artesanías de Colombia, Por la protección del legado Tule
sources.note: Full indexed institutional text: Caimán Nuevo and Arquía makers, agriculture/fishing historical subsistence, textile manufacture and income, geometric and figurative categories. Direct page fails.

sources.title: Banco de la República, Molas: Capas de sabiduría
sources.note: Direct/indexed museum educational page: Guna girls of Colombian Urabá and Panamanian Caribbean coast learn to sew designs for their blouses.

sources.title: Penn Libraries, Lenca vocabularies from Guajiquiro, Opatoro, Intibucá and Similiton
sources.note: Full indexed original catalogue: Berendt transcription of Squier lists, 84 words and numbers to 70, 1858 publication source, Guajiquiro collection June 1853. Direct catalogue intermittently fails.

sources.title: Eusebio Hernández and Alphonse Louis Pinart, Pequeño vocabulario de la lengua lenca (1897)
sources.note: Harvard library scan hosted on Wikimedia Commons. Original downloaded and locally rendered, printed page 4 / PDF page 10 visually inspected: Está lloviendo. / cuy gailainá. Historical Guajiquiro transcription, not a modern reconstruction. Cached PDF and PNG witness included.

sources.title: Editorial Guaymuras, Blanca Moreno García’s study of Rodrigo Ruiz’s testimony (2021)
sources.note: Direct publisher description of Y de la épica hazaña en memoria... La probanza sin pruebas de Rodrigo Ruiz. Identifies 1558 reward petition about 1537, contradictions and publication of 51 folios in 1987. Use only bounded description, not a claim to have read full book.

sources.title: Nancy Black, Investigaciones arqueológicas e históricas sobre los Lencas en Tencoa
sources.note: Direct 22-page IHAH article. Internal footer Yaxkin XV, November 1996 Extraordinary despite archive 1997 folder. Printed 127-128 mission sites and records, 130 school/music, 134-135 indigenous responses. Avoid generic examples from other regions.

sources.title: L. R. V. Joesink-Mandeville, Programa Arqueológico de Yarumela, temporada 1983
sources.note: Direct IHAH excavation report. Printed 16-17 tools and agricultural interpretation. Used as older regional archaeology only; report does not securely identify individual ancient households with later Lenca language. Cassava remains a possibility, not demonstrated.

sources.title: Lorena Yasmín Vásquez, La cultura Lenca (2024), Panorama UNAB 7
sources.note: Direct seven-page article, printed 20-26. Firsthand 2024 pottery documentation, printed 23 gourd tool/handles/polishing, 24 hot vessel and plant dye; page 25 records Potón Piau publication. Do not adopt unverified last-fluent-speaker claim or generalized extinction framing.

sources.title: National Museum of the American Indian, Lenca vessel 26/8930
sources.note: Direct/indexed museum catalogue: Honduras, made 2012, coiled/hand-built and slipped clay vessel, 30 by 21.2 cm. Purchase through gallery in 2012; unnamed maker, not excavated antiquity.

sources.title: Honduras Ministry of Education, Investigación Etnográfica del Pueblo Lenca
sources.note: Full indexed original printed 154, José Gabino Manuelles of Yamaranguila discusses Guancasco, musical instruments, school invitations and reciprocal village visits. Direct PDF fails. Reproducible query site.se.gob.hn/static/SDGEPIAH/files/DOCUMENTO_ETNOGRAFICO.pdf "Guancasco" "visita". Source calendar wording is inconsistent, so festival dates omitted.

sources.title: COPINH, Qué es COPINH (2008)
sources.note: Full indexed original organizational account, teacher training in coordination with Ministry of Education, rural access, local culture and language goals. Historical program account, no present enrollment claims.

sources.title: COPINH, Sanar es Resistir, 2018 women’s school record
sources.note: Full indexed original printed 118 documents eight meetings January-August 2018, women’s reflections, discussions and creative responses. Direct PDF fails. No remedies, dosage or medical efficacy claims drawn from recipe annex.

sources.title: COPINH, Semillas de libertad (2023)
sources.note: Full indexed original October 4, 2023 account of 2022 onward community gardens in Pueblo Viejo, El Achotal, Guachipilín and Montaña Verde, year-long training, organic fertilizer and food diversification.
